title: Dow Jones| Nasdaq | S&P 500 | US Stock Market Today |Live Updates: US markets turn green after Fed chief Warsh's speech at Jackson Hole - The Economic Times
text:
Dow Jones| Nasdaq | S&P 500 | US Stock Market Today |Live Updates: US stocks edged higher on Friday, led by gains in megacap shares, as Fed Chair Kevin Warsh reaffirmed the central bank's commitment to its 2% inflation target. Investors raised September rate-hike bets, while PayPal slumped on a reported abandoned takeover and Gap surged after lifting its profit outlook.

- Gary Schlossberg, global strategist, Wells Fargo Investment Institute, San Francisco

- Christopher Hodge, chief US economist, Natixis, New York

- Mark Hackett, chief market strategist, Nationwide, Philadelphia

Zinc fell from a four-year high on Friday after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's comments on inflation prompted traders to increase bets on a September rate hike. However, tight inventories continued to support prices, with LME zinc stocks falling to around two days of global consumption. Zinc remained on track for a 6.4% monthly gain in August.

The U.S. dollar index pared gains slightly after Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh’s comments at Jackson Hole, last up 0.06% at 99.16.

Marvell Technology fell 6.9% as investors questioned the timing of revenue from its AI chip agreement with Alphabet’s Google, despite an increased 2027 revenue forecast. PayPal dropped 15.4% after Bloomberg News reported that a consortium involving Advent and Stripe had abandoned its pursuit of the payments company. The moves added to a mixed premarket session for individual stocks, with investors balancing company-specific developments against broader concerns about rates and inflation.
